panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 11 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K). A: Panel A facial phenotype described in caption as SGBS coarse square face broad nose with cleft lip. B: Panel B facial phenotype of SGBS per caption. C: Carrier mother with supernumerary nipple, stated as common in SGBS carriers. D: Toddler with extra-nipple arrowed, SGBS manifestation. E: Close-up mouth showing large tongue per caption E,F,G group. F: Close-up mouth from SGBS patient in macroglossia group. G: Mouth close-up with teeth malposition and repaired cleft in SGBS patient, part of macroglossia series. H: Broad hand in SGBS per caption H and J broad hands. I: Deep plantar creases captioned as SGBS finding. J: Hand with polydactyly accessory digit visibly shown. K: Abnormal male genitalia with hypospadias captioned as SGBS finding.
panels.attribution_text: Tenorio et al. Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome types I and II.. Orphanet journal of rare diseases 2014. doi:10.1186/s13023-014-0138-0. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical findings in Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome. A and B: Facial phenotype. Note the cleft lip, coarse, square face and broad nose. C and D: extra-nipple in a carrier mother and a toddler. E, F and G: close up of the mouth of three different patients. Note the large tongue, middle groove in the tongue, teeth malposition and repaired cleft (in G). H and J: Hands. Note broad hands and polydactyly in one subject. I: Deep plantar creases. K: abnormal genitalia in a male with hypospadias and proximal anal placement. Written informed consent was obtained from the parents of the patients for publication of their photographs.
in_text_mentions: nose and lips are usually large and thick. Cleft lip and/or palate is observed in about 13% of cases. The tongue is wide and with a middle groove from the tip to the back of the tongue [9-11] (Figure 1). There may be midline minor anomalies such as subcutaneous lipomas, pits or flat nevus flammeus. Multiple odontogenic keratocysts were reported in one patient [12].Figure 1 Clinical findings in Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome. A and B: Facial phenotype. Note the cleft lip, coarse, square face and broad nose. C and D: extra-nipple in a carrier mother and a toddler. E, F and G: close up of the mou
Besides cardiovascular anomalies, supernumerary nipples are common in both affected individuals and carrier females (Figure 1).
Hypospadias, cryptorchidism and penoscrotal transposition have been observed in some individuals [22]. In one patient cryptorchidism also associated chordee of the penis (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Suspicion of congenital diaphragmatic hernia at 22 weeks of gestation

findings.label: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
findings.evidence: Suspicion of congenital diaphragmatic hernia at 22 weeks of gestation

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Prenatal ultrasound at 22 weeks gestation in fetus diagnosed with Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome; caption attributes striking profile to SGBS fetus, consistent with dysmorphic/coarse SGBS facies. B: Coronal fetal ultrasound with ocular measurements; part of A,B described as striking profile/brain structure in SGBS fetus, visually showing hypertelorism consistent with coarse facies with hypertelorism. C: Transverse fetal ultrasound with Doppler showing thoraco-abdominal defect; caption explicitly states suspicion of congenital diaphragmatic hernia in SGBS fetus, with in-text left-sided diaphragmatic hernia. D: Ultrasound shows increased subcutaneous fat tissue in SGBS fetus; in-text supports prenatal overgrowth with HC-AC-FL above 95th percentile and estimated fetal weight above 95th percentile, consistent with fetal macrosomia and overgrowth.
panels.attribution_text: Reischer et al. Simpson-Golabi-Behmel-Syndrome in Dichorionic-Diamniotic Twin Pregnancy.. Clinics and practice 2021. doi:10.3390/clinpract11010012. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Ultrasound at 22 weeks of gestation (A,B) Striking profile and brain structure in fetus with Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome. (C) Suspicion of congenital diaphragmatic hernia at 22 weeks of gestation and (D) increased subcutaneous fat tissue.
in_text_mentions: l estimated fetal weight of fetus II was above the 95th percentile and a nuchal fold of 8.1 mm with general oedema of the skin was present. The ultrasound scan additionally showed a striking profile (Figure 2). All measurements (HC-AC-FL) were above the 95th percentile. A suspicion of left-sided diaphragmatic hernia as well as hyperechogenic kidneys, increased in size and polycystic appearance, and a hypoplasia of genitalia have been identified. Furthermore, the scan revealed a polyhydramnios (DIP 10 cm). Due to the polyhydramnios of fetus II, fetus I has been compromised in a similar process

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of infant face from SGBS type 1 case report; caption explicitly states macrocephaly, macrostomia, and coarse facial features, matching vocabulary coarse facies finding.
panels.attribution_text: Zhang et al. Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome type 1 with subclinical hypothyroidism: A case report.. Medicine 2019. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000017616. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: The patient exhibited macrocephaly, macrostomia, and coarse facial features.
in_text_mentions: raniofacial features. Physical examination revealed coarse skin, and desquamate could be seen in the patient's wrinkles. The trunk and limbs had scattered red maculopapular rashes. The patient also exhibited macrostomia (Fig. 1), macroglossia, and hepatomegaly. The liver was 2 and 1 cm below the right costal margin and the xiphoid, respectively, and had a soft texture, as determined by palpation. The spleen was not palpated below the left costal margin. The anus opening was normal and hypertrophy was noted in the perianal fold. The fingers were thick, and the patient had postaxial polydactyly.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photo of adult SGBS patient (GPC3 variant mimicking acromegaly) showing captioned macroglossia with tongue protrusion, a vocabulary-defined SGBS manifestation. Attribution to SGBS not acromegaly per article title and in-text dysmorphic features list.
panels.attribution_text: Rishabh et al. Adult presentation of Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome due to a hemizygous <i>GPC3</i> stopgain variant mimicking acromegaly.. JCEM case reports 2026. doi:10.1210/jcemcr/luag115. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical photograph showing macroglossia with prominent tongue protrusion and partially widened dental spacing.
in_text_mentions: Dysmorphic features included hypertelorism, broad nasal bridge (Fig. 1), tubular nose, short philtrum, macrostomia, thick lips, mandibular prognathism, macroglossia (Figs. 2 and 3), broad hands with short distal phalanges, hypoplastic nails, genu valgum, lateral deviation of toes, and bilateral supernumerary nipples (Figs. 4).
